The system integrates vision and touch for active 3D shape reconstruction using a robotic hand with vision-based tactile sensors.
The active touch problem is formulated as selecting a sequence of grasps to minimize Chamfer Distance between predicted and ground truth shapes.
A high-resolution tactile simulator is implemented using PyBullet physics and Pyrender for rendering.
The reconstruction model uses a chart-based mesh representation deformed by two graph convolutional networks.
Positional embeddings and mask embeddings are used to encode vertex information in the mesh.
The simulator defines 50 grasp points uniformly distributed on a sphere around the object center.
The system was trained and evaluated on over 25,000 objects from the ABC dataset.
Data-driven active touch policies outperform random baselines by up to 18% in reconstruction accuracy.
Object-specific policies include Nearest Neighbor, Supervised regression, and Double Deep Q-Networks (DDQN).
Dataset-specific policies include Most Frequent Best Action (MFBA) and Lowest Error Best Action (LEBA).
The mesh autoencoder produces embeddings used to efficiently compute distances and train policies.
The simulator supports grasping with four fingers and poking with a single finger.
The reconstruction model can predict shape from touch-only or combined vision and touch inputs.
The framework enables learning active touch exploration strategies over large datasets, a first in the field.
The reconstruction pipeline is jointly optimized end-to-end to minimize Chamfer Distance.
The system achieves impressive reconstruction performance from single-view RGB images augmented with touch.
Touch signals improve reconstruction not only at the contact site but also extrapolate to local neighborhoods.
The framework runs efficiently with simulated grasps taking ~0.0317 seconds each on a Tesla V100 GPU.
The approach leverages learned object priors to guide exploration, unlike previous uncertainty-based methods.
The paper provides a novel formulation enabling vision-guided active touch exploration.
The mesh deformation model decouples object prior learning and refinement through two GCNs.
The reconstruction model uses perceptual feature pooling to project vision features onto mesh vertices.
The policies select grasps to maximize expected improvement in reconstruction accuracy.
The research bridges gaps between active vision, tactile sensing, and deep learning for 3D shape understanding.
